info.title: Releem API
info.description:
Manage servers and customers, inspect database diagnostics and retrieve performance metrics.

All example identifiers, addresses, names, query fingerprints and values are fictional. Replace them with values from your account.

Authenticate with an API token in the Releem-Secret-Key header. Internal Bubble integrations can instead supply an admin bearer token together with Releem-Bubble-Auth: true and the target user's Releem-Api-Key. Invalid, expired or revoked credentials return 401.

Errors use a JSON error object containing code, message and optional details.

get.description:
List event summaries for a server accessible to the authenticated user. Both time bounds are required and inclusive. Timezone offsets are converted to UTC; timestamps without a timezone are interpreted as UTC. Time bounds have one-second precision.

Results are ordered by event time descending, then event ID descending. Pagination is applied after server and time filters. The response contains `items`, without a total count; advance `offset` until a page contains fewer than `limit` items. Offset pagination does not freeze a snapshot: new events can shift subsequent pages.

get.description:
Server metadata with every health and security check of the latest report, passing or failing, in display order. Each check carries its result and its catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group.

Recognized security findings remain available when part of a report cannot be interpreted. Unresolved entries are returned in security_checks_unknown, and security_checks_decode_error describes any interpretation error. An empty security_checks object does not establish that all checks passed: inspect these fields. When no report is available, security_checks is empty and security_checks_decode_error is null.

Every health check of the server's latest report, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link and group. MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL servers have different checks. A check the catalog has no entry for is listed last with null texts.

Every security check of the server's latest security snapshot, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group. A check the catalog has no entry for is listed last with null texts. Check names follow the snapshot's engine: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL use separate catalogs. Account checks can fail with a null value when the producer did not include account details. Unsupported failure codes or mixed/ambiguous engine fields return `422 invalid_source_data`; they are not returned as an empty successful snapshot.

Every configuration state of one server, applied or not, newest first — the list Releem Platform shows. Each row is one state of a configuration, so a configuration that was applied or rolled back appears once per state; `configuration_id` groups them. All states are returned unless `limit` is given. With `latest=true` only the server's current state is returned — its newest state, the first row of the full list — or an empty list when the server has none.

get.description: Retrieve query execution statistics for a time window. The window is `[start_date, start_date + period)`, `[start_date, end_date)`, or the last `period` up to now without `start_date`. The start is included and the end is excluded in every mode. An explicit `end_date` requires `start_date` and overrides `period`; it must be later than the start. Bounds use second precision. Percentages are relative to every query that passes the filters, so with `schema_name` they are shares of that schema. The period is a positive integer optionally followed by `m` (minutes), `h` (hours), or `d` (days); a bare integer means days. Other suffixes are rejected.

parameters.name: period

schema.description: Positive integer with optional m (minutes), h (hours), d (days); bare numbers mean days
schema.title: Period

parameters.description: Positive integer with optional m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days). A bare integer means days. Default: 1 day. An explicit end_date overrides this duration; the period must still be valid.

parameters.name: start_date

schema.description: Window start, ISO date or datetime; without it the window ends now
schema.title: Start Date

parameters.description: Inclusive start, ISO date or datetime

parameters.name: end_date

schema.description: Exclusive window end, ISO date or datetime; requires start_date and overrides period
schema.title: End Date

parameters.description: Exclusive end, ISO date or datetime. Requires start_date, must be later, and overrides period.

parameters.name: timezone

schema.description: IANA time zone for start_date and end_date without an offset
schema.title: Timezone

parameters.description: IANA time zone for start_date and end_date without an offset; explicit offsets take precedence

schema.title: Query Filter

get.description: List available metrics for one server, including the server-scoped item ID needed for `GET /v1/servers/{id}/metrics/byId/{itemid}`.

Average, minimum and maximum of every metric of one server over a window, computed from hourly trends in one read. A metric without trend data in the window is listed with null values. `start_time` and `end_time` are required; a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range` and a window longer than 366 days with 400 `time_range_too_wide`. The window includes `start_time` and excludes `end_time`, so adjacent windows do not overlap; request two windows to compare a period with the previous one. Values that are not finite numbers are returned as null.

parameters.name: metric_name
parameters.description: The name of the metric to retrieve

schema.description: Aggregation function: avg, sum, min, max
schema.title: Aggregation

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Grouping interval: a positive number followed by m, h or d (e.g. 5m, 1h, 1d)

parameters.name: use_trends

schema.description: Use hourly trend summaries instead of raw samples
schema.title: Use Trends

parameters.description: Use hourly aggregated metric data instead of raw samples

get.description: Retrieve metric data for one server's metric, looked up by metric name. Unlike the deprecated `GET /v1/metrics/{metric_name}`, `start_time` and `end_time` are required and a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range`. Request parameters are validated before any data is read: `aggregation` must be one of the members below and applies only together with `interval` or `use_trends` (otherwise 400 `aggregation_requires_interval`); `interval` must look like `5m`, `1h` or `1d` (otherwise 400 `invalid_interval`). A window may span at most 31 days of raw samples, or 366 days with `use_trends=true` (otherwise 400 `time_range_too_wide`). Not every metric is aggregated into hourly trends; `use_trends=true` for an item that has no trend rows returns 400 `trends_not_available` rather than an empty series.

get.description: Retrieve metric data for one server's metric, looked up by its server-scoped item ID (from `GET /v1/servers/{id}/metrics`). `start_time` and `end_time` are required, and a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range`. An `itemid` that belongs to a different server returns 404. Request parameters are validated before any data is read: `aggregation` must be one of the members below and applies only together with `interval` or `use_trends` (otherwise 400 `aggregation_requires_interval`); `interval` must look like `5m`, `1h` or `1d` (otherwise 400 `invalid_interval`). A window may span at most 31 days of raw samples, or 366 days with `use_trends=true` (otherwise 400 `time_range_too_wide`). Not every metric is aggregated into hourly trends; `use_trends=true` for an item that has no trend rows returns 400 `trends_not_available` rather than an empty series.

Schema checks from the most recent completed run for one server. A null `timestamp` means no run has completed schema checks yet. A non-null `timestamp` with an empty `items` list means the filters matched nothing in that run — which equals "the run found nothing" only when no filters were applied.

The endpoint returns these check types only: `missing_primary_key`, `unused_index`, `duplicate_index`, `auto_increment`, `collation`, `character_set`, `table_engine` and `table_fragmentation`; any other value matches nothing

Title, texts, documentation link, severity and group of every health and security check, ordered by type, DBMS family and display order. The texts describe the check itself and are the same for every user and server. A server's results already include them: see `GET /v1/servers/{id}/health-checks` and `GET /v1/servers/{id}/security-checks`, whose check names match `key`.

The same `key` can appear once per DBMS family with different texts, so match on `type`, `dbms` and `key` together.

failed.description: Whether the check reports a problem.

value.title: Value
value.description: Observed check value; null when unavailable.

title.title: Title
title.description: Human-readable name of the check, or null when the catalog has no entry for it.

short_description.title: Short Description
short_description.description: One-line summary of the check for a table row, or null.
examples: How often a cached thread is reused.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the check examines and why it matters, or null when the catalog has no entry. Plain text; it contains no values of a particular server.
examples: Shows how often a new connection reuses a cached thread instead of creating one.

learn_more_url.title: Learn More Url
learn_more_url.description: Documentation link for the check, or null when there is none.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Importance of a security check: `critical`, `high` or `moderate`. Null for health checks and for checks without a catalog entry.

group.title: Group
group.description: Section the check is listed under, or null when it has none.

bearerAuth.description: Admin/Bubble bearer token. Enter the raw token only; Swagger adds 'Bearer ' automatically. Used with Releem-Bubble-Auth + Releem-Api-Key.

apiToken.name: Releem-Secret-Key
apiToken.description: Releem API token. Use this authentication method for API clients.

bubbleAuth.name: Releem-Bubble-Auth
bubbleAuth.description: Internal Bubble authentication flag. Enter true; requires bearerAuth and userApiKey.

userApiKey.name: Releem-Api-Key
userApiKey.description: Target user's API key for internal Bubble authentication; requires bearerAuth and bubbleAuth.

tags.name: Server Writes
tags.description: Writes for one server. Like the reads, every route requires the authenticated user to own the server named by `{id}` (canonical decimal form). Every write that passes body validation is recorded in the API audit log, including ones refused by the ownership or record checks. New tasks and query optimization records use the request processing time as their status timestamp. Updating a query optimization record does not change its status timestamp.

tags.name: Server Diagnostics
tags.description: Server-scoped read endpoints for one server's details, configuration history, query optimizations, metrics, deadlocks, agent tasks, processlist captures, and schema checks. All routes require the authenticated user to own the server named by `{id}`; an unknown or foreign server ID returns 404. `{id}` must be the canonical decimal form — `00101` or `abc` returns 404 on every route rather than being cast to a number.

tags.name: Checks
tags.description: Display texts for health and security checks. They describe a check itself, never one server's result.
